lucy: Quick notice: planned dry-run + policy change validation for dedicated-gpu pools on Thu 09/14 03:00-03:45 UTC. We're testing the new SLO-degradation policy (auto-leniency-tagging) and exercising the dedicated-pool failover play. No live routing changes; this is a canary/dry-run but we will execute capacity ops to simulate load. Please ack if you need to opt out. :mega:

raj: Ack. What's the exact scope of the policy change?

lucy: The change auto-applies a temporary SLO-leniency label on services in "maintenance" when the control-plane marks a region in test-mode. It prevents internal SLO burn alerts from firing while keeping external SLAs intact. We'll validate that labels propagate and alert suppression respects them.

devin: I'll own the label propagation checks and webhook tests. Adding a small script to assert label presence on all nodes.

oncall: I'll be oncall for the window. If anything looks like real degradation to customers, I'll halt. Criteria: customer 5xxs >0.2% or p99 >2x baseline.

runbook-bot: Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/eng-sre/dedicated-pool-failover-and-slo-policy. Preflight checklist included.

lucy: Preflight highlights (short):
```
# verify control-plane test-mode flag
redwood-admin config get --key region.test_mode --region us-central
# ensure SLO policy feature flag on
redwood-admin features list | grep slo-leniency-auto
```

raj: Preflight done: flags present, dedicated pool health OK. Scheduling synthetic load generator to target pool at 03:10 for 30m.

alert-bot: Calendar invite created: "Dedicated pool dry-run + SLO policy check" Thu 09/14 03:00-03:45 UTC. Attendees: eng-sre, eng-runtime, obs. Internal pager suppression configured for 60m window.

devin: Starting label-propagation dry-run now. Script output: all 42 nodes show label slo:leniency=test. Webhook delivery to alert-manager simulated and acknowledged.

oncall: Initiating synthetic load at 03:10. Ramp plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% for 10min steps. Watch for token-spike and KV miss storms.

monitor-bot: Ramp 10% complete: p95 +5ms, error 0. No internal SLO alerts triggered (suppress tag honored). External alerting unchanged.

monitor-bot: Ramp 50% complete: small p99 bump +30ms, internal alerts suppressed. Observed short-lived control-plane write latency spike. Investigating.

raj: Looking at control-plane metrics: leader election jitter due to GC pause on config-db replica. Temporary increase in control-plane write latency. Not customer impacting but could affect label propagation speed.

lucy: That's fine for dry-run. Note action item to add GC-tuning for config-db (raj). Proceeding to 100% ramp for validation.

oncall: At 100% we saw transient KV miss-rate increase to 6% for ~2m. No customer 5xxs. Deciding whether to exercise the failover playbook now (dry-run) or stop.

devin: Recommend exercising failover play steps but with --dry-run flag so we validate runbook flow without moving traffic. Example: `redwood-failover plan --pool dedicated-us-central --dry-run=true`

oncall: Doing the dry-run plan now. Runbook steps: preflight-verification -> promote-secondary -> canary-sim -> scale-secondary -> verify-kv-warmup -> finalize. All steps returned expected dry-run outputs.

monitor-bot: Dry-run canary simulation pass: latency p95 +12ms, errors 0. Webhook for SLO-leniency removal tested successfully.

lucy: Post-dry-run notes: SLO-leniency labels applied and removed as expected. Control-plane write latency issue is a follow-up. KV miss transient tolerated under leniency. No customer-facing impact. Action items: 1) raj: GC-tune config-db; 2) devin: add label-propagation end-to-end test in CI; 3) lucy: update runbook to document dry-run checklist.

oncall: I'll draft a short postmortem for the dry-run and file it to the runbook. If any of the action items look like they need immediate triage, ping me.

devin: Filing CI test RFC and starting work tomorrow.

raj: Scheduling GC-tuning patch review.

lucy: Thanks team. Please ack here when you've picked tasks. Quick sync 15m before live runs from now on. :eyes:
